subject: Re: Redwood integration — rate limits, retries & idempotency (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-13T16:05:00Z
Subject: Redwood integration — post-call recap & next steps

Alex — great call today, thanks for walking through Acme's ingestion pipeline and production constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

1) Priority items (next 2 weeks)
- SDK setup: we'll share a quickstart that includes API key setup and a Node + Python sample for streaming responses.
- Auth: confirm whether you'll use per-service API keys or a central service account (we recommend service account for server-to-server workloads).
- Routing & region: you asked about routing by latency and cost — we can pin inference to us-west for lowest latency and add fallback to us-east for capacity spikes.
- Structured output / tool calling: we'll demo function-calling for order-extraction and normalized JSON responses.
- Embeddings & rerankers: baseline is one embedding call per doc + in-memory FAISS reranker; we'll size requests to respect embedding rate limits.
- Rate limiting & retries: cover our recommended backoff & idempotency patterns (see below).

2) Rate limits / quotas (high-level)
- Hosted API has per-account token and request quotas (example: 60 requests/min for synchronous completions, 30 embedding requests/min for standard plan).
- Bursting is supported up to a short window; sustained throughput requires Dedicated capacity.
- We'll provide exact numbers for your trial account and map against your ingestion QPS.

3) Recommended retry & idempotency strategy (engineering notes)
- Respect 429/503 responses: read Retry-After header when present.
- Exponential backoff with jitter (base=200ms, factor=2, max=10s) for eligible requests.
- Only retry idempotent operations by default (embeddings, GET-like queries).
- For non-idempotent operations (e.g., commands that cause side effects), use an idempotency-key header (X-Request-ID or Idempotency-Key) so the server can deduplicate.
- Include a unique request ID on every client request (X-Client-Request-Id) for tracing; we'll log these on our side for debugging.

4) Client SDK behavior
- Our SDKs will: auto-inject Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>, set X-Client-Request-Id if not supplied, and optionally auto-retry only for idempotent calls with capped exponential backoff.
- We can enable 'safe mode' where the SDK attaches Idempotency-Key to chat/completion requests when you mark them safe to retry.

5) Deliverables (this week)
- Quickstart repo (Node + Python) with examples: streaming, function-calling, embeddings, and retry config. (attached)
- Diagram of rate-limit windows and example retry flow (attached).
- Short checklist for Prod cutover: key rotation, monitoring hooks, alert thresholds.

Next steps: can you share a rough QPS and expected tokens/day for your embeddings and chat paths? We'll match against the trial quotas and propose Dedicated sizing if needed.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>

Cc: Taylor Smith <taylor@acme.com>
Date: 2027-01-13T17:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Redwood integration — post-call recap & next steps

Ben — thanks for the recap, this is exactly what we needed. Quick answers:
- Expected embeddings QPS: ~12 qps, peak 20 qps during nightly batch windows.
- Chat generation (customer-facing): steady 8 rps, peak 25 rps.
- Tokens/day estimate: ~1.2M tokens/day across all services.

We prefer service account auth (automated rotation via our secrets manager). Region preference: us-west for latency.

Couple of follow-ups:
- Can the SDK automatically attach Idempotency-Key for chat messages that are retriable?
- For reranking, how do you recommend batching embeddings to stay under rate limits without adding too much latency?

I'll review the attachments and get you our internal network/egress requirements for private deployment next week.

—Alex

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-13T19:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Redwood integration — post-call recap & next steps

Alex — great, thanks for those numbers. Answers inline and some implementation guidance:

- SDK idempotency for chat:
  * We can provide an SDK flag `autoIdempotency=true` which will attach an Idempotency-Key for calls marked as "safeToRetry". It also preserves original request payload so retries include the same key. For cases where you can't safely retry (payments, DB writes triggered by the model), we'll surface a hook so your app can supply its own Idempotency-Key.

- Batching embeddings for rerankers:
  * Recommendation: micro-batching of 8–16 documents per request (tunable). This trades off latency vs. throughput — with 12 qps target, 8-doc batches give better CPU/GPU utilization and keep within per-minute embedding quotas.
  * If you need point-in-time freshness for reranking, use an asynchronous batching queue: push raw docs into the queue, produce embeddings with controlled concurrency, and update your vector store.

- Rate limits & retry details (more concrete):
  * Typical responses you'll see:
    - 200: OK
    - 429: quota exceeded or within short burst threshold — check Retry-After header (seconds) and X-RateLimit-Reset headers.
    - 503: transient backend capacity issue — treat similarly to 429 but prefer longer backoff.
  * Retry policy we recommend:
    - Eligible: embedding calls, read-only prompts, health-checks. Not eligible by default: chat messages that trigger side-effects.
    - Algorithm: exponential backoff with decorrelated jitter (e.g., sleep = random_between(base, min(cap, base * 2^attempt))). Base = 200ms, cap = 10s, max attempts = 5.
    - Honor Retry-After if provided: if Retry-After > next backoff, wait the Retry-After instead.
  * Idempotency: include Idempotency-Key header for operations that can produce side-effects (e.g., calls that write to your systems). Server will return 409 if duplicate with same idempotency key and conflicting state.
  * Request IDs & observability: always surface X-Client-Request-Id and we'll return an X-Server-Request-Id in responses. Share these IDs when escalating so we can find logs quickly.

- Operational notes:
  * Monitoring: set alerts for sustained 429 rate > 1% of calls and for rising median latency.
  * Backpressure: for peak windows, use a queue in front of the SDK and process at the allowed concurrency to avoid overwhelming the hosted endpoint.

Next actions on our side: Marissa to create a trial quota sheet mapped to your numbers; Rishi will prepare an SDK branch with `autoIdempotency` and sample config for embedding batching. Dev, can you draft a short example of the Idempotency-Key header usage in your architecture?

Cheers — Ben

On a side note, Taylor — since you handle security at Acme, we'll follow up with a short SOC 2 evidence packet if you want to start that thread.

From: Taylor Smith <taylor@acme.com>
